title: The Leap — Verified Research & Instrument Intelligence
description: Reproducible research layer for TradingView's The Leap paper-trading competition that separates official contest facts, historical champion outcomes, vendor-sourced market moves, capacity arithmetic and independently simulated strategy verdicts — and never presents a backtest as a platform result, never mixes real historical market returns with simulated competition returns, and never claims a figure comes from a real TradingView Strategy result. The audit banner at commit d09a594 is the twenty-second pass (2026-09-22): the thirteenth official frontier capture (R13, capture #11, 2026-09-22T23:00:00Z, 102,886 participants) recorded the edition's first rank-1 turnover, with HappyLittleTrades promoted to rank 1 at +1,193.11 percent / $2,982,777.45 and rank 50 at $1,525,023.75, rank 100 at $1,236,663.00 and rank 250 at $866,600.85 — all four frontiers up against R11, which supports H58 with +3,159 participants — while the displayed board proved non-monotonic between ranks 6 and 7, supporting H59 and logged as IR-37, and the landing counter read 102,883 against the displayed 102,886 (delta 3, IR-35 continuation). The rules were re-read line by line: the section-08 universe matches 94 of 94 symbols, caps and listing order with 0 equity instruments, the prize ladder is unchanged, and the >=$600 wire-only payment rail (IR-29) and the undefined MPT-Flawless names (IR-36) were re-confirmed. A full short-side eligibility re-read closes a standing question: the Mag7 rules carry no short, sell or borrow clause anywhere, and TradingView's official Paper Trading documentation publishes a side (buy/sell) field. Two new frozen futures models were rostered — F1 compressed-streak fade and F2 swing-failure reclaim, with 4 new usernames (StreakStan / CompressCleo, SpringSasha / CreekCasey) — taking the roster to 19 (16 contrarian plus 3 baselines), and a re-run at 2026-09-22T23:10:00Z over 456 participant-editions with the existing 15 PnLs byte-identical gave H56 supported (the F1 family mean beats the baseline mean on both prongs) and H57 refuted (the F2 family mean trails, though CreekCasey still printed the family's only >=5x edition at 6.636686x while ruining 8 of 24). The forward-test ledger grew the futures division (engine forward-ledger-2) to 229 usernames and 3,007 tranches, every username cross-checked against its latest_edition with all 229 within one cent per tranche and the stock divisions byte-identical to the prior engine. Hypotheses H56 to H59 take the register to 59 and sources to 110. data/full_pool_verdicts.json records 20 mechanical verdicts for H34-H39, H41-H43 and H45-H55 — 2 supported, 2 partially supported, 13 refuted and 3 inconclusive on zero fire (H39, H41 and H42). CME product hours are committed for all 20 pooled futures with a 196-date roll schedule built by 18 codecs, the 2 refusals being products with no codec (dates are never inferred from another product). The volatile-stock intraday matrix is complete at 60 of 60 equity series (20 each at 15m, 1h and 1d) with byte-level SHA-256 provenance in data/intraday_index.json, and the same index records 20 futures captures of which only COMEX:SIC1! landed. Captures remain Yahoo vendor-tier rather than exchange-verified: the Alpaca IEX route stays blocked on environment credentials, and the authenticated TradingView Strategy Report export is still blocked, so data/tv_benchmark.json reports blocked with the exact completion steps and its measured numbers come from a repository-written synthetic fixture. scripts/verify.py was executed here and reports 444 passed, 0 failed and 1 warning (IR-22, COMEX:SIC1! vendor close differing from the TradingView snapshot quote by 2.09 percent).

flags: Its own banner states the limit plainly: captures are Yahoo vendor-tier, NOT exchange-verified, official intraday acquisition is credential-blocked, the Alpaca IEX route needs authorized environment credentials, and no authenticated TradingView Strategy Report export exists. 'Do not treat historical candidates as current orders.'

The README's header banner and its body are out of step. The banner is dated 2026-09-20 and reports the completed 60/60 matrix, models C22 and C19-A and hypotheses H41 and H42, but those identifiers appear nowhere else in the document — the newest body section is still 'September 19 sixteenth pass', whose roster is 32 to 38 with C17-C19 and H37-H39, and whose audit banner note still describes the 37/60 partial pool. A reader taking the roster count or the verdict list from the body gets the previous state (IRR-59).

Most full-pool verdicts are negative or non-results rather than wins: H35 and H38 refuted, H34 and H37 only partially supported, and H39, H41 and H42 inconclusive because their models never fired on the full pool. A zero-fire model is reported as inconclusive, not as a pass.

Contest facts are re-verified rather than remembered, and discrepancies are registered instead of smoothed: the landing hero count (99,658) trails the contest count (99,663) by the usual async lag (IR-09), and the payment-rail text change is flagged as IR-29 with the payout config deliberately left at the older reading.
Read at commit 6d8f0ef, its fourth move inside two audits; the previous three were recorded at IRR-36 when the description was rewritten from R9 (96,707 participants) to R10 (99,663).
